articleTitle: “The condenser bushing.”
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Mr. President, gentlemen: Design engineers very frequently seem to find it necessary to pass high voltage conductors through a conducting medium, and in the accomplishment of their desires they make use of what are known as bushing insulators, That is, a hole is made through a conducting medium and it is bushed with some insulating material to protect the live conductor. Now, where the pressure handled is only a few thousand volts or so, the production of a suitable bushing insulator is a comparatively simple matter; a tube of porcelain, bakelite, or hard rubber fulfils the essential requirements. Where, however, the pressure runs into the hundreds of thousands of volts, it appears desirable to exercise a little more care and caution if we are to avoid all sorts of trouble from both a service and an expense point of view.

articleTitle: Some notes ok the manufacture of porcelain insulators
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Mr. President, gentlemen: It is more than probable that transmission engineers look upon porcelain insulators as an invention of the devil especially designed on scientific lines to lead them into temptation. With or without diabolical influence, however, some most disheartening interruptions of service have been occasioned in the past due to the inexplicable failure of line insulators which have been built up with what was undoubtedly an ample factor of safety. So serious did this insulation problem become about fifteen years ago that manufacturers throughout the world were compelled to undertake an intensive study of the behaviour of high voltage porcelain insulators.

publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: British Standard Specification for Ebonite for Electrical Purposes (B.S.S. No. 234 — 1933). The third edition of the B.S. Specification for Ebonite has recently become, available, and shows some interesting changes as compared with the 1931 edition. In the first place, the use of “accelerators” and loading materials is no longer prohibited, but excessive proportions of such substances are prevented indirectly by the. electrical tests. Consequently, although the composition of the ebonite is no longer specified, compliance with the tests ensures that the material is substantially composed of good quality raw rubber and sulphur.

publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Mr. President and Gentlemen, As there is a little more time available, I think it would be useful to show, through the epidiascope, a few illustrations showing the application of apparatus giving an alternating current arc. The first illustration shows a stationary type transformer welding plant for one operator, rated 12 kVA continuous or 16 kVA for one hour (the recognised time rating for welding units). This gives a welding capacity of 200 amps, when the secondary winding is arranged to give 80 volts on open circuit. To reduce the voltage immediately after striking the are, an adjustable reactance coil is used. The core is arranged with graduations of current, and is set to suit the particular size electrode to be used.

articleTitle: The congella power station of the electricity supply commission. a description and some operating expediences
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: At the time when the Electricity Bill of 1922 became law, the Durban Corporation were considering extensions to their electricity supply undertaking, and simultaneously the electrification of the railways from Durban to Maritzburg was being investigated. The Electricity Supply Commission, by virtue of the powers granted to it under the Act, proposed to erect a power station at Durban to meet the requirements of both the Corporation and the Administration Negotiations with the Durban Corporation reached a satisfactory conclusion, but the electrification of the railway line between Durban and Maritzburg did not materialise. The result was that the Commission proceeded with the planning of Congella Power Station alter a satisfactory agreement with the Corporation had been negotiated and a promise had also been obtained from the Administration that power would be taken from the Commission when the line to Maritzburg was electrified. The station was designed with this end in view.

These lines interconnect the Witbank Power Station with the Company's Witwatersrand System at Brakpan. It is not considered necessary to give details of the Company's system or the capacity of its plant, beyond mentioning that the maximum demand to date on the System is 350,000 kW.; it should be noted that the paper is in no way based on short-circuit values or any data other than purely fault statistics and relative information extracted from the 132 kV line fault records.

abstract: Mr. President and gentlemen: In reply to Mr. A. Heydorn's remarks, the authors agree that the overload characteristics are of such a nature that in some eases it might prove undesirable to operate the machine over this range for any considerable time. It should be remembered, however, that the machine is essentially a synchronous type motor which, by virtue of the induction motor characteristics, is able to start up against lull load torque, and is prevented from shutting down completely in the event of an overload being imposed upon it. The asynchronous range is not an operating range in the true sense; it is merely an emergency range.

articleTitle: The electrical extraction and refining of metals

abstract: At the outset I feel that an apology is due for the character of this paper. Written at the suggestion of your Council and with a time limit, it must necessarily partake rather of the character of a lecture than of a technical paper. Nevertheless, the subject is doubtless sufficiently outside the ordinary “beat” of most electrical engineers for an account of the manner in which electricity is utilised for these purposes to be of some interest. It is perhaps hardly necessary to say that both the heating and electro-chemical effects of electrical currents are employed in electro-thermal and electrolytic methods respectively, and for convenience the subject is often dealt with under these two heads.

abstract: The authors are to be congratulated on the presentation of this paper, in which their investigation into the efficiency of the steam raising plant has been exhaustive, but, unfortunately, very little is given regarding the turbine room. Referring to the operating statistics for the month of September, 1932, the average steam and vacuum conditions are practically in accordance with the designed figures for the turbines. Correcting the thermal efficiency item (8) into terms of units generated, we obtain 20-2 per cent. Taking the boiler house efficiency as 81 per cent., it follows that the turbine efficiency is 24.9 per cent. compared to the guarantee figure of 28.2 per cent. There is insufficient data available, however, to enable constructive criticism to be made with respect to the large discrepancy.

articleTitle: New and revised British standard specifications
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: British Standard Specification for Insulating Oils for Electrical Purposes (B.S.S. No. 148 — 1933). The British Standard Specification for Insulating Oils is quoted in practically every contract in this country for transformer and switch oil, and any revision of the specification is, therefore, a matter of very general interest. The 1933 edition of the specification embodies no changes as regards the physical properties of the oil — a testimony to the soundness of the technical basis of the previous edition — but introduces a new test for freedom from moisture. The old edition specified that the oil should be “sufficiently free from moisture” to satisfy the requirements of the specification, but apart from the electric strength test there was no criterion of freedom from moisture. An additional test, in the form of at “crackle“ test, has now been incorporated, but owing to the somewhat unscientific nature of this test it is regarded as optional only, to be applied only when so specified by the purchaser. As the result of experience in the application of this test it is hoped that a definite technique may be evolved, thus enabling a more scientific test to be established than is at present possible.

articleTitle: Annual banquet
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: (The Council of the Institute is indebted to the Editor of the Rand Daily Mail for permission to reproduce the newspaper report of the Institute's Annual Banquet.) The Annual Banquet of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers was held on Friday, 10th November, 1933, at the Carlton Hotel, Johannesburg, and proved to be one of the outstanding functions of the year. Mr. Charles J. Monk, the President of the Institute, presided. The attendance numbered 279, and included the Hon. N. C. Havenga, Minister of Finance, the Hon. Patrick Duncan, K.C., C.M.G., Minister of Mines, and the Hon. A. P. J. Fourie, Minister of Labour, Commerce and Industries.

articleTitle: Factors affecting the design of turbo generators
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: General. Mr. President and gentlemen, with your kind permission, instead of rending the paper as such, I will give a descriptive lecture, using slides based on the subject matter. The operation of turbo generators is associated with guarantees of temperature and electrical characteristics. The temperatures of the machine are dependent upon the heat to be dissipated, i.e., the losses; the thermal conductivity of the materials; the cooling surface and efficiency of the ventilating system, whilst the electrical characteristics are primarily a function of the magnetic and electric loadings associated with the excitation.
